questions.passage_text:
The following table shows the sales data of five products (A, B, C, D, E) across four quarters of a year:

Product | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4
A       | 120| 140| 160| 180
B       | 200| 180| 220| 240
C       | 150| 160| 140| 170
D       | 100| 120| 110| 130
E       | 80 | 90 | 100| 110
questions.question_text: Which product showed the highest percentage increase from Q1 to Q4?
questions.solution_text: Calculate percentage increase for each product: A: (180-120)/120 × 100 = 50%, B: (240-200)/200 × 100 = 20%, C: (170-150)/150 × 100 = 13.33%, D: (130-100)/100 × 100 = 30%, E: (110-80)/80 × 100 = 37.5%. Product A has the highest percentage increase at 50%.
questions.full_markdown:
### Question

**Data Table:**
Product | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4
A       | 120| 140| 160| 180
B       | 200| 180| 220| 240
C       | 150| 160| 140| 170
D       | 100| 120| 110| 130
E       | 80 | 90 | 100| 110

**Question:** Which product showed the highest percentage increase from Q1 to Q4?

**Options:**
- A. Product A
- B. Product B
- C. Product D
- D. Product E ✅

Delhi      | 55    | 50      | 30
Bangalore  | 40    | 65      | 35
Chennai    | 35    | 55      | 20
questions.question_text: Which city has the highest total smartphone sales across all three brands?
questions.solution_text: Calculate total sales for each city: Mumbai: 45+60+25 = 130, Delhi: 55+50+30 = 135, Bangalore: 40+65+35 = 140, Chennai: 35+55+20 = 110. Bangalore has the highest total sales at 140 thousand units.
